rows.subtype: Approach: decide a personal rule that only diversified index-style options are used [Thinking]
rows.description: The person writes a short investing policy: small regular amounts, only regulated products, nothing that promises fixed high returns. A pre-set rule removes the need to judge each pitch in the moment.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: cutting losses, impulsive action, inversion

rows.subtype: Approach: trust a persuasive relative's tip without checking [Pitfall]
rows.description: A cousin, sincere but misled, recommends a scheme that pays for recruiting others. Trust in the person is confused with trust in the scheme, and the student nearly joins.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: cutting losses, inversion

rows.subtype: Approach: learn the basics of returns and risk first [Thinking]
rows.description: The student reads a beginner guide from a regulator's investor education site, and learns that higher returns carry higher risk. Basic knowledge makes false promises easier to spot.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: cutting losses, impulsive action, inversion

rows.subtype: Approach: sort out runway with a cash and expense count [Thinking]
rows.description: After a layoff at a startup, the employee counts savings, essential monthly costs and expected severance to see how many months of runway exist. The number turns a vague fear into a bounded problem.

rows.subtype: Approach: cut non-essential costs and pause loan EMIs by talking to lenders [Action]
rows.description: The person cancels subscriptions, moves to a cheaper phone plan and calls lenders about temporary relief on payments. Reducing outflow buys time to search without panic.

rows.subtype: Approach: take the first offer accepted out of panic [Pitfall]
rows.description: Fearing the gap, the employee accepts a role with lower pay and a poor fit without asking about terms. Within three months the person is looking again, showing how fear can override checking the match.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning, avoidance and procrastination, emotion-aware planning, forward planning, lateral thinking, negotiation

rows.subtype: Approach: structured job search with weekly targets [Action]
rows.description: The employee sets a weekly plan: update the CV, apply to ten roles, message five former colleagues and practice one mock interview. A routine gives a sense of progress even when replies are slow.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning, avoidance and procrastination, emotion-aware planning, lateral thinking, negotiation

rows.subtype: Approach: hide the news from family to avoid worry [Pitfall]
rows.description: Ashamed, the person continues leaving home each morning and tells no one. The secrecy adds stress and cuts off leads, advice and emotional support that relatives could have offered.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning, emotion-aware planning, forward planning, lateral thinking, negotiation

rows.subtype: Approach: reframe the layoff as a chance to upskill [Thinking]
rows.description: The person asks what the market values, picks a cloud certification and a part-time freelance gig to keep income coming. Reframing does not remove worry, but it directs energy to steps that add to future options.

rows.subtype: Approach: seek support from a peer network and a counsellor [Action]
rows.description: The person joins an alumni group of laid-off colleagues, shares openings and mock-interview time, and speaks to a counsellor when the mood is low. Support is treated as part of the plan.
